faqSection.title: Questions About Studying in Australia
faqSection.description: Find answers to common questions about Australian university admissions, English tests, student visas, part-time work and living costs.

faqs.question: Can I study in Australia without IELTS?
faqs.answer: IELTS is not the only English language test accepted by Australian universities. Many institutions accept alternatives such as PTE Academic, TOEFL iBT, OIETC and Cambridge English, depending on their admission policies. Duolingo is not universally accepted, so students should check the specific university requirements.

faqs.question: How long can I stay in Australia after completing my studies?
faqs.answer: Eligible international graduates may apply for the Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485), under the Post-Higher Education Work stream. The source lists general periods of 2 years for Bachelor's degrees, up to 4 years for Master's by Coursework, up to 2 years for Master's by Research, and up to 4 years for doctoral degrees. Applicants must meet the relevant age, qualification and visa requirements.

faqs.question: Can international students work part-time while studying in Australia?
faqs.answer: International students holding a valid Student Visa (subclass 500) can generally work up to 48 hours per fortnight while their course is in session. During official course breaks, they can work unlimited hours, subject to visa conditions. Different entitlements may apply to Master's by Research and doctoral students.

faqs.question: What are the main university intakes in Australia?
faqs.answer: Australian universities generally offer February/March and July intakes. Some universities also offer additional intakes in November or other months, depending on the course and availability.

faqs.question: What is a Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE), and when do I receive it?
faqs.answer: A Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE) is an official electronic document issued by an Australian education provider after you accept your admission offer and complete the required enrolment steps. In most cases, students must accept the offer, pay the required tuition fee deposit and arrange OSHC before receiving the CoE. It is required for an Australian Student Visa (subclass 500) application.

faqs.question: How much money do I need to show for an Australian student visa?
faqs.answer: Students must demonstrate sufficient funds for tuition fees, living expenses, OSHC and travel costs. The source lists AUD 29,710 for 12 months of living expenses for a single student, in addition to first-year tuition, OSHC and travel expenses. Financial evidence may include bank deposits, scholarships or acceptable financial sponsorship.

faqs.question: Can I bring my spouse or family members to Australia?
faqs.answer: The supplied content states that, under Australian Student Visa rules effective from 2 October 2026, most international students can no longer include a spouse or dependent children in their Student Visa (subclass 500) application or generally bring them later as subsequent entrants. It lists limited exemptions for certain PhD students, DFAT or Defence-sponsored students, eligible foreign-government scholarship recipients, and eligible nationals of certain Pacific Island or ASEAN countries. Bangladesh is not included in the Pacific Island or ASEAN exemption. Check the latest Department of Home Affairs requirements before making plans.

faqs.question: Can I study in New Zealand without IELTS?
faqs.answer: The supplied content states that an English proficiency test score is mandatory for international applicants and that New Zealand universities no longer accept MOI waivers. Alternatives listed are PTE Academic (50+ for undergraduate and 58+ for postgraduate, with no communicative skill below 42/50), TOEFL iBT, and Cambridge C1/C2 Advanced.

faqs.question: How long can I work after completing my studies?
faqs.answer: Eligible graduates may apply for a New Zealand Post-Study Work Visa. The duration and permitted work depend on the qualification completed in New Zealand. Eligible Master's and doctoral graduates who studied full-time in New Zealand for at least 30 weeks may qualify for up to 3 years. Other qualifications can have different eligibility and visa durations.

faqs.question: Can international students work part-time while studying?
faqs.answer: Eligible international students may be allowed to work up to 25 hours per week during study and full-time during scheduled holidays. The exact conditions depend on the student's visa, course and education provider. Students must check their eVisa conditions before starting work.

faqs.question: What are the main university academic intakes?
faqs.answer: The main New Zealand intakes are Semester 1 in February/March and Semester 2 in July/August. Some programmes also offer rolling or trimester entry. The supplied content recommends applying 6–9 months before the intended start date.

faqs.question: What is an Offer Letter and when do I receive it?
faqs.answer: After submitting all required documents, the university or education provider issues an Offer Letter. The supplied content estimates 2–8 weeks for a complete application and states that tuition payment is not required at this initial stage. Students can lodge a Student Visa application with Immigration New Zealand using the Offer Letter. Tuition fees may be paid before visa lodgement or after receiving Approval in Principle (AIP). Once payment is confirmed and conditions are met, INZ issues the electronic visa (eVisa).

faqs.question: How much bank solvency funds do I need to show for the visa?
faqs.answer: For tertiary-level study lasting one year or more, Immigration New Zealand requires evidence of NZD 20,000 per year for living costs, or NZD 1,667 per month for study shorter than one year. Tuition fees must be covered separately. The evidence and acceptable funding arrangements depend on the application.

faqSection.description: Find answers to common questions about Malaysian university admissions, English tests, Student Pass applications, part-time work and living costs.

faqs.question: Can I study in Malaysia without IELTS?
faqs.answer: IELTS is not the only English-language qualification accepted by Malaysian universities. Some institutions accept alternatives such as TOEFL iBT, PTE Academic or other recognised evidence. Certain universities may offer English preparatory programmes. Requirements depend on the institution and selected course.

faqs.question: Can international students work part-time while studying in Malaysia?
faqs.answer: Eligible international students at public universities and private higher education institutions may apply for permission to work part-time for up to 20 hours per week during semester breaks or holidays exceeding seven days. Prior approval from the Immigration Department is required, and work is restricted to permitted locations and sectors. Students should confirm the current rules with their institution and Immigration before accepting work.

faqs.question: Can Bangladeshi students stay and work in Malaysia after graduation?
faqs.answer: Malaysia's Graduate Pass is available only to nationals of specified eligible countries. Bangladesh is not included in the currently published eligible-country list. Bangladeshi graduates should not assume they qualify for this pass and should check the latest Immigration and Education Malaysia guidance for any alternative employment or residence route.

faqs.question: What are the main university intakes in Malaysia?
faqs.answer: Many Malaysian universities offer intakes around February or March and September or October. Some institutions and programmes have additional intakes during the year. Availability depends on the university, course and study level.

faqs.question: How does the Malaysia Student Pass process work?
faqs.answer: After receiving an offer from an authorised institution, the Student Pass application is coordinated through the institution and EMGS. Eligible applications proceed to eVAL approval. Applicants from countries requiring an entry visa must follow the applicable Single Entry Visa process. After arrival, new students must complete the required medical screening within seven working days and proceed with Student Pass endorsement through their institution.

faqs.question: How much does it cost to study in Malaysia?
faqs.answer: Tuition fees vary by institution and programme. As an indicative planning range, many Bachelor's programmes may cost around MYR 15,000–45,000 per academic year, while monthly living expenses may be around MYR 1,100–2,850. Medicine and other specialised programmes may cost considerably more. Students should obtain an official fee quotation and budget separately for insurance, visa-related charges and travel.

faqs.question: Can I bring my spouse or family members to Malaysia?
faqs.answer: Dependant eligibility depends on the student's level of study, institution and Student Pass category. Certain higher education Student Pass holders may be eligible to apply for dependant passes under Immigration rules. Approval is not automatic, and dependants are not permitted to work under dependant pass conditions. Confirm eligibility with the institution and Immigration before making plans.

faqs.question: Are Malaysian university degrees internationally recognised?
faqs.answer: Many Malaysian universities and international branch campuses offer qualifications recognised in other countries. Recognition depends on the institution, programme accreditation and the requirements of the country or professional body where the qualification will be used. Students should verify the programme's accreditation before applying.

faqSection.title: Questions About Studying in the United States
faqSection.description: Find answers to common questions about U.S. university admission, English tests, student visas, costs and work authorisation.

faqs.question: What student visa do I need to study in the United States?
faqs.answer: Most students pursuing academic programmes at SEVP-certified schools apply for an F-1 student visa. Vocational or other study programmes may have different visa categories. The institution should confirm the appropriate category and issue the required documentation.

faqs.question: What is Form I-20?
faqs.answer: Form I-20 is the Certificate of Eligibility for Nonimmigrant Student Status issued by an SEVP-certified school after it accepts an eligible student and completes the required review. Students use the form as part of the F-1 visa application and entry process.

faqs.question: Do I need IELTS or TOEFL to study in the USA?
faqs.answer: Many universities require proof of English proficiency, but accepted tests and minimum scores vary. Some institutions accept IELTS, TOEFL, PTE Academic or Duolingo English Test, while others may grant an exemption or offer an English pathway. Check the selected programme's current policy.

faqs.question: Can international students work while studying in the USA?
faqs.answer: F-1 students may generally work in qualifying on-campus jobs up to 20 hours per week while school is in session, subject to applicable rules. Off-campus work requires a specific authorisation category, such as eligible CPT or OPT, and students must obtain the required approval before starting.

faqs.question: Can I work in the USA after graduation?
faqs.answer: Eligible F-1 graduates may apply for post-completion Optional Practical Training (OPT), generally up to 12 months. Graduates with qualifying STEM degrees may be eligible for a 24-month STEM OPT extension if they meet all applicable requirements. OPT is not automatic and requires proper authorisation.

faqs.question: How much does it cost to study in the United States?
faqs.answer: Costs vary widely by institution, programme and location. As an initial planning estimate, tuition may range from around USD 8,000–20,000 per year at some community colleges, USD 20,000–50,000 for many undergraduate programmes and USD 20,000–55,000 for selected graduate programmes. Living costs, insurance, fees and travel are additional. Always use the university's current cost-of-attendance estimate.

faqs.question: What are the main intakes in U.S. universities?
faqs.answer: Many U.S. institutions offer Fall intake, usually beginning around August or September, and Spring intake, often beginning around January. Some institutions also offer Summer or other entry terms. Programme availability and deadlines vary.

faqs.question: How much bank balance do I need for an F-1 student visa?
faqs.answer: There is no single fixed bank-balance amount for every U.S. student visa applicant. The student should be prepared to document credible funding for the costs shown by the institution, including tuition and living expenses for the relevant period. The consular officer assesses the applicant's circumstances and supporting evidence.

faqs.question: Can I get a scholarship as an international student?
faqs.answer: Some U.S. institutions offer merit scholarships, need-based aid, graduate assistantships, fellowships or athletic awards to international students. Eligibility and availability vary, and funding is competitive. Students should check scholarship deadlines and whether awards cover tuition, living costs or both.

faqs.question: Can I bring my spouse or children while studying in the USA?
faqs.answer: Eligible F-1 students may have a spouse and unmarried children under 21 apply for F-2 dependent status. Each dependent needs the required documentation from the school and must meet visa requirements. F-2 dependants have restrictions, including that an F-2 spouse may not work.

faqSection.description: Find answers to common questions about Canadian admission, study permits, finances, student work and post-graduation options.

faqs.question: Do I need IELTS to study in Canada?
faqs.answer: Many institutions require proof of English or French proficiency, but accepted tests and minimum scores vary by institution and programme. Some institutions may offer exemptions based on prior education. Check the exact admission requirements.

faqs.question: What is a Designated Learning Institution (DLI)?
faqs.answer: A DLI is a school approved by a provincial or territorial government to host international students. You generally need a letter of acceptance from a DLI to apply for a study permit. PGWP eligibility is separate, so check the institution and specific programme.

faqs.question: Do I need a PAL or TAL for a Canadian study permit?
faqs.answer: Most study permit applicants need a provincial or territorial attestation letter. Exemptions apply to certain groups; from January 1, 2026, students in degree-granting master's or doctoral programmes at public DLIs are exempt. Always check the current IRCC rules for your situation.

faqs.question: How much money do I need to show for a study permit?
faqs.answer: You must show funds for tuition, living expenses and transportation without relying on work in Canada. IRCC updates the required living-expense amount periodically and the amount depends on family size and study location. Check the official financial-support page before applying.

faqs.question: Can international students work while studying in Canada?
faqs.answer: Eligible students may work off campus up to 24 hours per week during regular academic sessions and full-time during scheduled breaks, provided they meet the study permit conditions. Not every student or programme qualifies.

faqs.question: Can I get a Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP) after studying?
faqs.answer: Possibly. You must graduate from a PGWP-eligible programme at an eligible DLI and meet all applicable requirements, including language and, for some non-degree programmes, field-of-study rules. A DLI's status alone does not guarantee PGWP eligibility.

faqs.question: How long does it take to process a Canadian study permit?
faqs.answer: Processing times vary by country, application volume, completeness, biometrics and other factors. Check the official IRCC processing-time tool for the latest estimate; no fixed processing time can be guaranteed.

faqs.question: Can I study in Quebec?
faqs.answer: Yes. Quebec has universities and colleges offering programmes in English and French. Applicants may need a Quebec Acceptance Certificate (CAQ) and must follow Quebec-specific financial and immigration requirements, subject to applicable exemptions.
